session.ownerChanged: You are now signed in as a different user. The screen was reopened for that user.
session.ownerChangedRelogin: You are now signed in as a different user. Please sign in again.

auth.logoutStayed: Could not sign out. You are still signed in.
auth.logoutUnverified: Could not confirm your sign-in state. Please try again in a moment.

grid.inlineEditErrorHint: In the input, Tab reads the error and Enter retries. In the error, Shift+Tab or Escape returns to the input.
grid.columnsMenuLastColumn: The last visible column cannot be hidden

validation.max: Enter a value of at most {max}

dashboard.pipelineTotalNote: Adopted estimates of {count} pre-order projects ({missing} without an amount are excluded)
dashboard.pipelineWeightedNote: Sum of amount × probability ({missing} without a probability are excluded)
dashboard.attentionNote: Missing estimates, no adopted version, or a missing / mismatched revenue plan
dashboard.demoNote: Demo mode has no aggregates. The project ledger and customers show fictional data.
dashboard.linkPipeline: Pre-order estimates, probabilities and order months
dashboard.linkProjects: Register projects, convert orders, recognize revenue
dashboard.workspaceCaption: Your own memo; input stays until you save. Drag the panel out to float it - the layout is saved automatically.
dashboard.panelMemoBody: Edit and save the memo in the dashboard’s Memo panel.
dashboard.memoPlaceholder: Type a memo. Until you save it, the text stays even when you move or dock the panel.
dashboard.memoSaveFailed: Could not save the memo. Your text is kept.
dashboard.memoChangedWhileSaving: Text typed while saving has not been saved yet.
dashboard.memoCloseBody: The memo has unsaved text. Save it before closing?

auth.tagline: Bring your business data into one admin console.
auth.setupNote: This is the first launch. Create an administrator account.
auth.loginNote: In Tauri/LAN mode, log in with the account you created at first launch.
auth.demoNotePrefix: The standalone browser (demo) mode lets you log in with
auth.passwordTooShort: Enter a password of at least 8 characters
auth.setupUnsupported: This environment does not support initial setup
auth.skipLoginNote: For a small single-device app. Anyone at this device will be able to use it. You can switch to login-based operation later under Settings → Security.
auth.skipLoginFailed: Failed to start without a login
settings.pageDescription: Configure this device's behavior: theme, LAN access, backups, and more.
settings.themeDesc: Switch the preset and display density. The color mode is switched with the sun/moon button in the header.
settings.themeNote: Settings are saved to this device immediately, and while you are logged in they are also saved to the settings DB (Tauri/LAN server) and shared with other clients (spec §12.1 / M12).
settings.navLayoutDesc: Show the page links in a sidebar on the left or in a dock at an edge of the screen.
settings.launcherOpaqueNote: Your OS is set to reduce transparency, so the dock is shown opaque.
settings.languageDesc: Choose the display language for the admin UI.
settings.languageNote: Switching languages reloads the page so every screen updates. Your choice is saved to this device and, while you are logged in, to the settings DB (M12).
settings.kioskDesc: Collapses the sidebar, makes the header compact, and shows a fullscreen button (for a permanently-mounted dashboard).
settings.vibrancyDesc: Rendering behind the desktop app window (Windows only).
settings.vibrancyNote: Render behind the window with the OS acrylic (frosted glass) effect. Combined with the glass preset, it becomes real glass that lets the desktop show through (M12, Windows only).
settings.lanDesc: Let browsers on other devices on the same LAN use this screen.
settings.viewerPublicToggle: Allow LAN viewing without a login (viewer-public)
settings.viewerPublicNote: Anyone on the LAN can use the viewer screens and read-only API without logging in. Writes still require a login.
settings.lanDisabledByAuth: While login-not-required mode is on, LAN access can only be enabled together with viewer-public.
settings.explicitSaveHint: Changes on this screen take effect only when you press "Save and apply" (Appearance & Language settings are applied and saved as soon as you pick them).
settings.savedValuesUnavailable: The saved settings could not be loaded, so they cannot be changed. Please reload.
settings.scopeLanRunning: Running, reachable from devices on the same network
settings.lanUiNotEmbedded: This build does not include the web UI for other devices, so the connection check from another device is not available (the distributable installer built with `tauri:build:windows` includes it; for development, run `pnpm build` and then build with `--features embed-ui`).
settings.lanReachabilityNote: Depending on firewall or router settings, a device on the same network may still be unable to connect.
settings.ipv6NotGuidedRunning: Running (IPv6 binds are not guided to a connection address)
settings.ipv6NotGuidedNote: This bind address is IPv6, so this screen does not guide to a connection URL or QR code for it.
settings.serverDesktopOnly: Server settings can only be changed in the desktop app.
settings.lanNote: When enabled, browsers on other devices on the same LAN can use the same screen via the REST API + SSE (spec §11). Enable it only on a trusted LAN.
settings.firewallHeading: Information needed to allow it through the firewall
settings.firewallDesc: If devices on the same network cannot connect on Windows, allow incoming connections with the details below. They describe the server that is listening now.
settings.firewallNotNeededStopped: The server is not listening, so no firewall setting is needed.
settings.firewallNotNeededLocal: The server is listening on this PC only, so no firewall setting is needed.
settings.firewallRemoteNote: "LocalSubnet" covers the subnets of every network connection of this PC, including VPN connections.
settings.firewallCommandsDesc: Run one of these in PowerShell started as administrator, or pass it to your administrator. If a rule with the same name already exists, the command stops with a warning and changes nothing (it never removes or rewrites an existing rule).
settings.firewallCommandProgramNote: Covers every TCP port this app listens on, so the rule keeps working after a port change.
settings.firewallCommandPortNote: Covers any program listening on this port. After changing the port or switching forms, the administrator checks the existing rule with Get-NetFirewallRule -Name '<rule name>' | Format-List and updates or removes it themselves (remove with Remove-NetFirewallRule -Name '<rule name>').
settings.firewallCommandsUnavailable: The commands could not be built because the app identifier is unavailable. Use the details above to add the rule.
settings.firewallRuleExists: A firewall rule named {name} already exists, so nothing was changed. Check it with Get-NetFirewallRule -Name '{name}' | Format-List, then update or remove it yourself.
settings.firewallCopyStale: The listening server changed, so nothing was copied. The details above are updated; check them and copy again.
settings.firewallCopyUnavailable: The server state could not be read, so nothing was copied.
settings.firewallCopyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
settings.firewallBlockNote: A blocking rule wins over an allow rule (for example after choosing not to allow the app in a Windows notification). If it still cannot connect, ask your administrator to check.
settings.firewallVendorNote: Security software with its own firewall, or a centrally managed company PC, may still block connections allowed in Windows. Give the details above to that product's settings or to your administrator.
settings.firewallStatusDesc: Checks, by reading only, whether Windows Defender Firewall has the rules the commands above create (looked up by their names). Nothing is changed.
settings.firewallStatusDiffers: Present, but different from what the command creates:
settings.firewallStatusLocalUnknown: The local rule of this name could not be read.
settings.firewallStatusLocalDiffers: The local rule of this name has other values, which do not apply:
settings.firewallStatusLocalMissing: There is no local rule of this name on this PC.
settings.firewallStatusPolicy: The rule of this name in the active store (ActiveStore) comes from central management ({kind}; source: {source}), not from this PC's local rules; that policy decides what applies.
settings.firewallStatusOrigin: The rule of this name in the active store (ActiveStore) is not this PC's local-store rule but {kind} (source: {source}).
settings.firewallStatusOriginUnknown: Where the rule of this name in the active store (ActiveStore) comes from is unknown (its source type was not reported; source: {source}).
settings.firewallSourceDynamic: a rule added at run time (Dynamic)
settings.firewallStatusUnconfirmed: Present (values as expected, but whether it is applied could not be confirmed)
settings.firewallEnforcementUnread: Enforcement unknown (EnforcementStatus could not be read)
settings.firewallStatusNotEnforced: Present (values as expected, but not applied as a Windows Firewall rule)
settings.firewallEnforcementCategoryOff: Another firewall product is on, so the rule is not applied as a Windows Firewall rule. Some products also evaluate Windows rules. Check whether connections arrive with the connection check from another device, and if they do not, allow the port in that product's settings.
settings.firewallStatusGroupUnknown: Whether the group {group} has rules with other names could not be checked.
settings.firewallStatusUnavailable: Could not check the Windows Firewall status.
settings.firewallStatusChanged: The server changed while checking. Check again.
settings.firewallStatusGroupOther: The group {group} also has {count} rule(s) with other names.
settings.firewallStatusReachNote: A rule being present does not mean other devices on the LAN can connect: security software with its own firewall, other rules that block the port (including centrally managed ones), and router or Wi-Fi settings can still block it. Only the rules with these names are checked here.
settings.firewallChangeDesc: Once you approve the Windows prompt (User Account Control), a helper program adds or removes the per-executable rule with administrator rights. This works only when the app is installed under Program Files.
settings.firewallChangeDescAllow: Otherwise, to allow it, run the command above in an administrator PowerShell.
settings.firewallChangeDescRemove: Otherwise, to remove it, run Remove-NetFirewallRule -Name '<rule name>' in an administrator PowerShell, or delete the rule in Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security.
settings.firewallChangeWaiting: Waiting for the answer to the Windows prompt (User Account Control). If you cannot see the prompt, check the taskbar.
settings.firewallChangeDenied: You are not allowed to change the firewall (only administrators can).
settings.firewallChangeUnavailable: The result of the firewall change could not be received. Check the state shown above.
settings.firewallChangeStale: The server state changed during the change. The result below is about the previous target. Check the state shown above again.
settings.firewallChangeDoneRemove: The allow rule was removed (or there was none).
settings.firewallChangeAlreadyAllow: The allow rule is already in place. Nothing was changed.
settings.firewallChangeAlready: The rule is already as requested. Nothing was changed.
settings.firewallChangeConflict: A rule with the same name that this app did not create exists, so nothing was created or removed. It may be managed by another app or an administrator. Check what that rule contains in Windows Defender Firewall's advanced settings, and leave the decision on it to an administrator.
settings.firewallChangePolicy: Central management such as Group Policy keeps this PC's local rules from applying. A change may still have been made (for example, a rule created and then not applied). Check the state shown above and ask your administrator.
settings.firewallChangePrecondition: The permission cannot be changed from here with this installation.
settings.firewallChangeCancelled: The Windows prompt (User Account Control) was cancelled. Nothing was changed.
settings.firewallChangeLaunchFailed: The helper program could not be started.
settings.firewallChangeUsage: The helper program did not accept the request. The app and the helper program may be different versions.
settings.firewallChangeUnexpectedExit: The helper program ended with an unexpected result.
settings.firewallChangeTargetChanged: The server state changed after the confirmation was shown, so nothing was done. Check the state shown above and try again.
settings.firewallChangeBusy: Another firewall change is running, so nothing was done. Try again when it has finished.
settings.firewallChangeUnknownOutcome: The app returned a result this screen does not know. Check the state shown above.
settings.firewallChangeNoPrompt: No Windows prompt (User Account Control) was shown.
settings.firewallChangeManual: You can also allow it by running the administrator command above in an administrator PowerShell.
settings.firewallChangeManualRemove: You can also remove it yourself: in an administrator PowerShell, run Remove-NetFirewallRule -Name '<rule name>', or delete the rule in Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security.
settings.firewallChangeReach: A rule being present does not mean other devices can connect. Check with "Connection check from another device" below.
settings.firewallRefusalNotUnderProgramF: The app is not installed under Program Files (portable copies, per-user installations and moved copies are not supported).
settings.firewallRefusalHelperMissing: The helper program is not in the same folder as the app's executable.
settings.firewallRefusalLayout: The installed files are not laid out as expected. Reinstall the app.
settings.firewallRefusalReparsePoint: The installation path contains a junction or a symbolic link.
settings.firewallRefusalOwner: A file or folder of the installation is owned by someone other than Administrators, SYSTEM or TrustedInstaller.
settings.firewallRefusalWritable: A file or folder of the installation can be modified by users other than administrators.
settings.firewallRefusalUnverifiable: The access rights of the installation could not be verified.
settings.firewallRefusalIdentifierMismat: The app's identifier does not match the helper program's (possibly a rename that was not applied to both).
settings.firewallRefusalUnsupported: Not available on this OS (Windows only).
settings.firewallRefusalHelper: The helper program decided that the installation cannot be trusted.
settings.firewallRefusalUnknown: The installation could not be verified.
settings.firewallConfirmAllowPorts: This allows ALL TCP ports this executable listens on, from private networks.
settings.firewallConfirmAllowSubnet: The source range "Local subnet" may include the subnet of each network adapter or VPN when the PC has more than one.
settings.firewallConfirmRemoveScope: Only the per-executable rule this app created is removed. A rule of the same name this app did not create, and the per-port rule, are not removed.
settings.firewallConfirmUac: When you continue, the Windows prompt (User Account Control) appears. If you approve it, a helper program runs with administrator rights.
settings.reachDesc: Open the check URL on another device (a smartphone, for example) to record that it reached this PC's server. This check is separate from the firewall information and rule status.
settings.reachUnreadable: Could not read the check status.
settings.reachUnverified: No connection from another device has been checked yet.
settings.reachPending: Scan the QR code or open the URL on another device. Opening it on this PC does not count.
settings.reachPendingNoUrl: This check URL was issued before this screen was opened, so it cannot be shown. Issue a new one if needed.
settings.reachSelfAccess: The URL was opened from this PC itself ({time}). That does not count as another device.
settings.reachStale: This check was a while ago. Check again if needed.
settings.reachVerifiedNote: This confirms that this device reached the server at that time. It does not guarantee that other devices or routes can, or that it still can now.
settings.reachExpired: No other device opened the URL before it expired.
settings.reachExpiredNote: This does not prove it cannot connect (the URL may just not have been opened). Check the following, then issue a new URL.
settings.reachHintNetwork: The device is on the same network as this PC (same Wi-Fi / subnet)
settings.reachHintFirewall: This PC's firewall (on Windows, the firewall information and the Windows Firewall status above)
settings.reachHintVendor: Security software with its own firewall
settings.reachHintIsolation: Whether the Wi-Fi access point keeps devices apart (client / AP isolation)
settings.reachChanged: The server changed while issuing, so no URL is shown. Issue it again.
settings.reachIssueFailed: Could not issue a check URL.
settings.reachRefusedNotListening: The server is not listening, so no check URL can be issued.
settings.reachRefusedUnsupportedBind: No check URL can be issued for the current listen address.
settings.reachRefusedLoopbackOnly: The server listens on this PC only, so other devices cannot connect. No check URL can be issued.
settings.reachRefusedUnknownHost: The selected address is not one of the current listener's URLs. Refresh and select again.
settings.reachRefusedStaleGeneration: The server changed while issuing. Issue it again.
settings.reachRefusedLocalAddressesUnava: This PC's addresses could not be determined, so no check URL can be issued.
settings.reachScopeNote: This only checks that a device reached the server at that time. A check URL works once and expires in a few minutes. Changing the listen settings clears the results.
reach.title: Connection check
reach.recorded: The connection from this device was recorded. Check the result on the PC.
reach.selfAccess: This was opened from the PC itself. Open it on another device (a smartphone, for example).
reach.unusable: This URL cannot be used (expired, already used, or the server's listener changed). Issue a new URL on the PC.
reach.hostMismatch: This is not the right URL. Open the URL (or QR code) shown on the PC exactly as it is.
reach.rateLimited: Wait a while, then try again.
reach.noToken: This URL cannot be used (it has no check information). Scan the QR code shown on the PC, or open its URL exactly as it is.
reach.failed: Could not check. Issue a new URL on the PC and try again.
reach.note: This check does not log in or use the app. You can close this page.
settings.firewallFieldActiveNo: not applied (a policy keeps local rules from taking effect)
settings.firewallReasonQueryFailed: reading failed, e.g. a permission or a central management policy
settings.firewallReasonUnreadableOutput: the result could not be read
settings.portFallbackStarted: Port {requestedPort} was in use, so LAN access started on port {port}. Port {port} will also be used from the next launch.
settings.portFallbackNotSaved: Port {requestedPort} was in use, so LAN access started on port {port}, but the new port could not be saved. Save a port under Settings > Server & Connectivity.
settings.portFallbackExhausted: LAN access could not start: port {requestedPort} is in use, and so is every port up to {lastPort}. Choose another port under Settings > Server & Connectivity.
settings.portFallbackNoUsablePort: LAN access could not start: port {requestedPort} is in use, and no usable port was found up to {lastPort} (some are in use or reserved by the OS). Choose another port under Settings > Server & Connectivity.
settings.autologinDesc: Automatically log in with a specified account at startup (desktop only).
settings.autologinUnneeded: Auto login is not needed in login-not-required mode.
settings.autologinNote: Credentials are stored in the OS keyring. This account is logged in automatically at startup.
settings.auditDesc: Set the retention days and row cap for automatically tidying records.
settings.auditNote: Entering 0 makes that item unlimited (defaults are 90 days / 100,000 rows). Old records are tidied automatically when the list is shown. You can view the record list from the "Audit log" screen.
settings.systemInfoDesc: Check the running version and database status.
settings.systemInfoNote: Read-only diagnostics. The session count is an upper bound and may include expired-but-not-yet-swept sessions.
settings.authDisableDesc: Use this device without a login screen. A high-impact operation.
settings.authDisableNote: Enable it only if you completely trust this device. LAN access can only be combined with it if viewer-public is enabled.
settings.authDisableConfirm: Enabling login-not-required mode lets anyone who opens this device operate without logging in. Continue only if you completely trust this device.
settings.passwordChangeUnavailableAuth: In login-not-required mode there is no account, so the password cannot be changed.
settings.passwordChangeUnsupported: This environment does not support changing the password.
backup.heading: Backup / restore
backup.desc: Create database backups and restore from them.
backup.postgresNotice: Built-in backup/restore is SQLite-only. For PostgreSQL, back up with pg_dump and restore with pg_restore.
backup.note: Creates an online backup in the backups/ directory next to the DB file (VACUUM INTO, safe while running). Restore verifies the uploaded/selected file (integrity check + schema check), stages it, and applies it automatically at the next startup (it never swaps the running DB). The current DB just before applying is backed up automatically (spec M17).
backup.restoreConfirm:
{source}

The current data is backed up automatically when applied. A restart is required to apply. Continue?
backup.openFolderUnsupported: Not supported on this OS. Open it manually: {path}
audit.pageDescription: A record of user actions and system events.
audit.unavailableDesc: Not available in demo mode. The standalone browser demo mode has no audit-log DB, so this feature is available only in the Tauri app or via LAN access (embedded server).
audit.retentionNote: Retention policy: up to {days} / up to {rows} (change it on the "Settings" screen)
audit.recordCountNote: There are {count} records. Click a row to show details below.
audit.notLoadedNote: The audit log could not be loaded.
audit.loadError: Failed to load the audit log
audit.loadTimeout: The server did not answer within {seconds} seconds.
audit.boundaryMismatch: The server read a different range of records than the one requested.
audit.malformedResult: The server's answer was not in the expected form.
audit.snapshotExpired: Older records were deleted by the retention policy while the list was loading. Reading on would shift the rows, so loading has stopped. Use "Reload" to read the current records again.
audit.reloadNote: The list shows the records as of when it was loaded. Use "Reload" to include newer records.
users.pageDescription: Create, edit, delete accounts and reset passwords.
users.unavailableDesc: Not available in demo mode. The standalone browser demo mode has no account DB, so this feature is available only in the Tauri app or via LAN access (embedded server).
users.createDesc: Create an account by specifying a username, password, and role.
users.listDesc: Click a row to show the edit panel on the right.
users.editDesc: Update the display name and role.
users.resetDesc: Set a new password and force it onto this user.
users.deleteDesc: Delete this account permanently. This cannot be undone.
users.selectHint: Click a row in the list to show the edit panel here.
uiDemo.intro: The main states of the @banto/ui components (shown in the nav only in demo mode).
uiDemo.header.desc: Heading, description and actions. This page's own heading is a PageHeader with a description and actions.
uiDemo.card.desc: A section surface. Combinations of title, description, body and footer.
uiDemo.badge.desc: A default icon per variant. Never relies on color alone - an icon is always drawn.
uiDemo.iconButton.desc: `label` becomes aria-label and title. Sizes: md (default) and sm.
uiDemo.menu.desc: The menu parts. Opens from a trigger, moves with Arrow keys / Home / End, closes on Esc, outside click or Tab.
uiDemo.menu.label: Sample menu
uiDemo.palette.desc: The command palette. Arrow keys select, Enter runs. While open, focus is trapped inside; closing with Esc or an outside click returns focus to the opener.
uiDemo.palette.label: Sample palette
uiDemo.overlay.desc: A centred modal and a right-edge drawer. Esc closes one layer at a time, topmost first; while open, focus is trapped inside, and closing returns focus to the opener. With text entered, the drawer does not close on Esc or a backdrop click (use ×).
uiDemo.overlay.modalBody: For one-way tasks that need no surrounding context, such as creating something.
uiDemo.overlay.drawerBody: For editing next to the list. Typing in the field below counts as unsaved changes.
uiDemo.overlay.openNested: Open a confirm modal on top
uiDemo.overlay.nestedBody: Press Esc and only this modal closes first.
uiDemo.overlay.blocked: You have unsaved input. Press × to close.
uiDemo.toast.desc: Toast notifications (the app-wide store and ToastHost). Colour and announcement follow the kind (success and info are status, error and warning are alert); a toast with an action runs it on click and closes.
uiDemo.empty.title: No data
uiDemo.empty.description: Change the conditions and try again.
uiDemo.error.title: Failed to load
uiDemo.error.description: Please try again in a moment.
uiDemo.loading.desc: A skeleton plus an announced label (aria-live). The caller supplies the label.
cost.forbiddenDesc: You have not been granted access to this content. Ask an administrator if you need it.
cost.notFoundDesc: The record does not exist or cannot be shown.
customers.description: Register customers. Customers no longer in use are not deleted; clear "In use" instead.
projects.description: The project ledger. Only projects you may view are listed.
projects.emptyDesc: There are no projects you can view yet.
projects.managerIdHint: The manager is given by user ID (a new project starts with your own).
projects.orderedStatusHint: An ordered project's status moves only between ordered, in progress and work done (settling goes through the close-out check).
pipeline.description: Aggregates the latest adopted version of each pre-order project. Unset values are never treated as 0; they are counted instead.
pipeline.demoUnavailable: The pipeline is only available with the server or the desktop app.
pipeline.totalsNote: Projects with no amount or probability are left out of the weighted total and counted instead.
pipeline.monthsNote: Order months and revenue months are different views; do not add the two tables together.
pipeline.revenueExcluded: {count} projects with no amount or probability are not included by revenue month.
pipeline.sectionForbidden: You don't have access to this project's pipeline.
pipeline.adoptConfirm: Adopt v{no}? The aggregate will use this version.
pipeline.orderedNotice: Ordered projects take no new pipeline versions (handled by order changes).
pipeline.newVersionDesc: Every save creates a new version; earlier versions are never rewritten. Saving as adopted requires a basis.
pipeline.planDesc: Enter planned revenue per month. Mark amounts with no timing yet as "Timing undecided".
pipeline.errorNonNegativeInteger: Enter a whole number of 0 or more
pipeline.errorBasisRequired: An adopted version needs a basis
pipeline.errorPlanAmount: Plan amounts must be whole numbers of 0 or more
pipeline.errorPlanMonth: Enter a plan month or mark it as timing undecided
orders.sectionForbidden: You are not allowed to see this project's order and revenue amounts.
orders.forbiddenAction: You are not allowed to do this.
orders.beforeOrder: This project is not ordered yet. Convert it to an order to record the confirmed amount and revenue plan (no revenue is recognized automatically).
orders.notConvertible: A project in status "{status}" cannot be converted. To revive a lost or cancelled project, change its status first.
orders.convertDesc: The same project switches to ordered with the order date, confirmed amount, basis and revenue plan. The last pipeline version stays as history and leaves the pre-order aggregate.
orders.convertConfirm: Switch project {code} to ordered? It cannot go back to a pre-order status.
orders.remainderDesc: The part not ordered becomes a new pre-order project with an adopted pipeline version, so the ordered part is not also left in the pipeline.
orders.remainderOf: Remainder of a partial order. Original project:
orders.orderedPlanDesc: Spread the confirmed amount over the months revenue is expected (or timing undecided). The total must equal the confirmed amount.
orders.totalsNote: Confirmed amount = conversion + approved changes. Unconfirmed additions are not part of it or of the profit.
orders.replanDesc: Re-spread the amount not yet recognized over months (or timing undecided). The total must equal the unrecognized remainder; cleared amounts stay.
orders.changesDesc: Record the difference and its basis. Until approved it is an unconfirmed addition; approval adds it to the confirmed amount and to the revenue plan of its month.
orders.approveConfirm: Approve order change {no} and add it to the confirmed amount and the revenue plan?
orders.recognitionsDesc: Record revenue accounting approved (needs the revenue capability). It clears the plan automatically, starting with the month recognized, so planned and recognized revenue are never counted twice. Mistakes are cancelled with a reason.
orders.cancelPrompt: Reason for cancelling the revenue recognized on {date}
orders.errorPositiveAmount: Enter a whole number of 1 or more
orders.errorPlannedDates: Planned start and end are required once ordered
orders.errorPlanLines: Enter a month (or timing undecided) and an amount of 0 or more for each line
outlook.description: Per month: recognized revenue, ordered revenue plan, and pre-order revenue weighted by probability. Never added to the order-month figures.
outlook.viewingSnapshot: Showing the saved snapshot "{label}" ({at}) with the figures as saved.
outlook.tableNote: Timing-undecided amounts are their own row and are never spread over months. Unconfirmed additions are not in the outlook. This is not booked revenue or the company's accounts.
outlook.excludedTitle: Projects left out (amount or probability unset, or no adopted version)
outlook.issuesTitle: Projects whose plan does not match the remainder
outlook.snapshotNote: Saves the current outlook of every project (needs the company-report capability). Later conversions or recognitions do not change it.
outlook.snapshotForbidden: Saving a snapshot needs the company-report capability.
calcBasis.description: Company calc basis: hourly cost rates, the day length, alert thresholds and more. A change is added as a new version with an effective date; earlier versions stay in the history. Per-project overrides are made on the project page.
calcBasis.demoUnavailable: The calc basis is not available in demo mode
calcBasis.onNote: Shows the values that apply on this date
calcBasis.noHistory: No value has been recorded yet (unset)
calcBasis.changeDesc: Adds a new version with an effective date. Earlier values are not rewritten and stay in the history. Check the impact before saving.
calcBasis.errorReason: Enter the reason for the change
calcBasis.forbiddenChange: You are not allowed to change this item
calcBasis.impactBefore: Value on the effective date now
calcBasis.impactPending: Records costed with the new value on approval
calcBasis.impactCorrections: Approved records to review for correction
calcBasis.impactClosed: Records in closed months are included. Handle them with the post-close correction procedure.
calcBasis.impactNote: Approved hours and costs, adopted forecasts and approved budgets do not change automatically.
calcBasis.projectDesc: The values that apply to this project. An override affects this project only; other projects and the company basis do not change.
